idea.title: Uber-style on-demand dog walking app (GB)

source.text: An Uber-style app for on-demand dog walking that takes 20% of each walk. Launch country GB, budget 5,000 GBP, 15 hours a week, goal startup, edge: I am a developer. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug dog-walking-app.

idea.problem: Dog owners need a walker at short notice and want to book one instantly.
idea.solution: An Uber-style mobile app that matches dog owners with nearby walkers on demand.
claims: An Uber-style app for on-demand dog walking
assumptions: Customer assumed to be working dog owners in dense UK cities, London first, because the input names no segment.
Walk price assumed at the Rover London 30-minute average of GBP 14.19; the 20% take is the user's.
Launch in one London area first; the user gave GB only.
No existing audience, walker network or validation, since the input mentions none (headless run, no questions asked).
Interest in the domain assumed neutral: the stated goal is a startup and no pet-care background is given.

confidence.note: Raise it with real UK CPC for 'dog walker near me' (Keyword Planner) and on-demand repeat-booking data; both are estimates here.

gross_margin.note: 20% of a GBP 14.19 walk = GBP 2.84; Stripe card, Connect payout and account fees leave about 77% margin (estimate).

ltv_cac.note: LTV about GBP 26 vs CAC about GBP 40 per owner (estimate): 0.65. R4: regulars who would fix it leave the platform.

pricing_power.note: Rover UK takes 15%, and 5% on recurring care; 20% is above the leader and off-app the take is zero. Lowered by R4.

build_effort.note: Two-sided app with live GPS, Stripe Connect, vetting and dispatch: 2-4 months at 15 h/week (estimate).

skills_match.note: Developer covers the build; walker recruitment, vetting and local ops are new skills.

capital_needed.note: GBP 5,000 covers app fees, DBS checks at GBP 20 each and one area's launch, with little margin for paid acquisition.

time_to_mvp.note: About 12 weeks to a working two-sided app plus vetted walkers in one area (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Owners book same-day; walker onboarding (DBS, insurance) takes weeks.

channel_readiness.note: No audience or walker network; liquidity type check hit: on-demand needs idle walkers within minutes in every district.

search_demand.note: 10.2M-15.5M UK dogs and 49% of London households own one; demand for walks is large, for on-demand walks unproven.

trend.note: Mixed: UK Pet Food says a record 15.5M dogs (2026), PDSA says 10.2M, down from 11.1M (2025).

willingness_to_pay.note: Owners pay GBP 12-15 per London walk on Rover; they pay the walker, not for on-demand speed.

free_alternatives.note: Local Facebook groups, Nextdoor and BorrowMyDoggy's free tier cover matching; payment and trust are not free.

competitor_density.note: Rover (27k UK App Store ratings), Tailster, BorrowMyDoggy, Airtasker, Pawshake; one dominant leader.

differentiation.note: 'On-demand' is the only difference, and the best-funded on-demand player (Wag, USD 300M raised) went bankrupt.

legal_regulatory.note: Council licences and 4-6 dog caps vary by borough; Uber-style control raises worker-status risk (Uber v Aslam, 2021).

platform_dependency.note: Needs App Store and Play, but guideline 3.1.3(e) exempts physical services from in-app purchase fees.

market_risk.note: Walking is a durable, recurring need; the on-demand format is the fragile part.

skills.note: Strong on the build, no stated marketplace or pet-care operations track record.

assets.note: No audience, walker network or local partnerships stated.

interest.note: Goal is a startup; no domain interest stated (assumption).

tam.reasoning: UK paid dog walking spend: low 10.2M dogs x 5% walked x 2 walks/wk x 52 x GBP 13; high 15.5M x 10% x 3 x 52 x GBP 15

sam.reasoning: Platform-takeable London share: TAM low GBP 690M x 15% London share (assumed) x 20% take

som.reasoning: 0.1% of SAM GBP 20.7M for a solo founder in year 1

competitors_found.reasoning: Rover, Wag (US), Tailster, BorrowMyDoggy, Airtasker, Pawshake, plus free Facebook groups and Nextdoor

price.reasoning: 20% take x GBP 14.19 Rover London 30-min average walk (sourced)

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Assumed: occasional on-demand users plus regulars moving off-platform; lifetime 1 / 0.125 = 8 months

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Assumed click to first booking for an unknown brand on Meta; no UK marketplace benchmark found

cac.reasoning: Owner: Meta ~GBP 0.50/click / 2% = GBP 25; plus GBP 15 share of walker acquisition and vetting

ltv.reasoning: Net take GBP 2.18 x 1.5 walks/month x 8 months

payback_months.reasoning: CAC 40 / (2.18 x 1.5 = 3.27 gross profit per month); longer than the 8-month lifetime

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Apple developer GBP 79/yr ~6.6 + hosting ~20 + tools and domain ~23; excludes founder time and ads

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: 50 / 3.27 = 15.3, rounded up; ignores acquisition spend, which never pays back

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: ~150 h build at 15 h/week = 10 weeks, plus 2 weeks to vet the first walkers

verdict.launch_reason: The user's country; London has the highest share of dog-owning households (49%) and the densest demand.

type_checks.note: On-demand needs idle walkers within ~15 minutes in every district; a Wag executive called finding one nearby hard. Supply must come first.
Rover UK cut its fee to 5% on weekly recurring care; sitters openly take clients off-platform.

verdict.cheapest_test: Landing page and 20 DMs offering existing UK walkers a GBP 19/month booking-and-payments tool; pre-sell founding seats in 7 days.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 5 walker calls booked from 40 messages by day 5 -> stop
Fewer than 3 paid founding seats at GBP 19/month by day 7 -> stop
Fewer than 10 waitlist sign-ups from walker groups by day 7 -> stop

rescue.change: Sell a GBP 19/month booking, payments and walk-report tool to existing UK walkers instead of a marketplace.
rescue.why: Removes liquidity and disintermediation; fixes ltv_cac and pricing_power with a subscription the walker keeps.
rescue.requires: Access to walker groups such as the NarpsUK Sitters Forum on Facebook

rescue.change: Run a managed walking service in one London postcode: recruit 3-5 walkers, sell recurring weekly packages yourself.
rescue.why: Fixes channel_readiness and disintermediation by owning the client; becomes a service, not a startup.
rescue.requires: Time for local operations beyond 15 h/week once it grows

rescue.change: Build a cover network where walkers hand off clients when sick or on holiday, taking a fee per covered walk.
rescue.why: Uses walkers as supply and demand at once; partly fixes liquidity, but volume per walker is low.
rescue.requires: A dense walker community in one city

narrative.answer: **NO-GO**. Rover already owns UK dog walking at a 15% fee, 5% on recurring walks, so a 20% on-demand app is undercut on price and loses its regulars off-platform. **LTV:CAC of 0.65** means every customer costs more than they bring.
tldr: Rover dominates UK walking with 27k App Store ratings and charges less than your 20%.
On-demand walking was tried at scale: Wag raised USD 300M and went through Chapter 11 in 2025.
The demand is recurring and trust-based, so walkers and owners skip the platform after the first walk.

key_findings.title: Rover undercuts the 20% take
key_findings.detail: Rover UK charges **15%** on one-off bookings and **5%** on weekly recurring care, so your fee is the highest in the market.

key_findings.title: On-demand dog walking already failed
key_findings.detail: Wag, the original 'Uber for dog walking', filed a prepackaged **Chapter 11** in July 2025 after net losses every year.

key_findings.title: Customers cost more than they earn
key_findings.detail: Net take of GBP 2.18 per walk at 1.5 walks a month gives an LTV of about GBP 26 against a CAC of about GBP 40: **LTV:CAC 0.65** (estimate).

narrative.recommendation: Do not build the on-demand app. Spend 7 days pre-selling a GBP 19/month booking and payments tool to existing UK dog walkers; build only if 3 pay.
narrative.steelman: UK dog ownership is near a record (**15.5M dogs**, 2026) and hybrid work creates short-notice gaps a developer could fill cheaply. Evidence: owners want a trusted regular walker, not speed, and Rover already serves short-notice bookings.
narrative.lesson: In trust-based local services, the relationship belongs to the provider, so a per-transaction cut only survives on the first booking.

premortem.cause: Walkers and owners met on the app, then moved regular walks to bank transfer to dodge the 20% fee.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 30% of first-time owners book a second walk in-app within 30 days

premortem.cause: Too few idle walkers per district, so on-demand requests went unfilled and owners churned.
premortem.early_signal: Under 70% of requests filled within 60 minutes in the launch area

premortem.cause: Owners already on Rover saw no reason to switch to a pricier, emptier app.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 20 owner sign-ups from 1,000 local ad clicks

changes.what: Wag, the flagship on-demand walking app, filed for Chapter 11 and was taken private by its lender.
Blackstone took Rover private for about USD 2.3bn, consolidating the category leader.
Tower Hamlets set a GBP 240 professional dog walker licence with a 4-6 dog cap.
UK Pet Food reported a record 15.5M dogs, while PDSA reported a fall to 10.2M.
NarpsUK says hybrid work puts more pressure on short-notice walks, without figures.

why_now.note: The on-demand wave peaked in 2015-2019; its leader went bankrupt and the category consolidated, so the window is closed.

icp.who: Working dog owners aged 25-44 in inner London on hybrid schedules, with one dog and no regular walker
icp.pays_for_today: A regular walker at GBP 12-15 per 30-min walk on Rover in London, or about GBP 450/month for 5 walks a week
icp.trigger: Back to the office on set days, or the regular walker cancels or goes on holiday

free_alternative.evidence: UK owners are told to find walkers via local Facebook groups and a free meet-and-greet; BorrowMyDoggy offers free volunteer walks with a free basic tier.

strong_competitor.evidence: Rover UK has 27k ratings at 4.9 on the UK App Store and was bought by Blackstone for about USD 2.3bn in 2024; Tailster, BorrowMyDoggy and Airtasker also serve UK walks.

graveyard.evidence: Wag filed Chapter 11 in July 2025 after net losses of USD 17.6M (2024); London's DogBuddy was absorbed by Rover in October 2018.

no_distribution.evidence: Clear for the first 10: local Facebook groups and Nextdoor reach owners at near-zero cost; paid CAC of GBP 30-150 on Google (GBP 1.50-3 CPC) exceeds occasional-user value.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Clear: Stripe UK 1.5% + 20p and Connect 0.25% + 10p payouts leave about 77% of the GBP 2.84 take; Apple 3.1.3(e) exempts physical services from IAP.

weak_demand.evidence: Clear but mixed: 15.5M dogs and 41% of households (UK Pet Food, 2026) against 10.2M (PDSA, 2026); demand for walks holds, for on-demand it is unproven.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Clear with friction: no national licence, but borough licences (Richmond, Tower Hamlets, Royal Parks) cap dogs at 4-6, and Uber v Aslam (2021) raises worker-status risk.

saturated_wave.evidence: About 9 dog-walking-related launches in 2026 (e.g. PetMeet on Product Hunt), but only 2-4 are walker marketplaces; under the 10 threshold.

customer.segment: Working dog owners in inner London on hybrid schedules
customer.pain: Needing a walk on office days or when the regular walker cancels
customer.today: A regular local walker found via Facebook groups, Nextdoor or Rover, at GBP 12-15 per 30-min walk

use_cases.name: Last-minute walk when the regular walker cancels
Recurring weekday walks for office days
use_cases.effort: Medium, but walkers take it off-platform

use_cases.name: Booking, payments and walk reports for walkers

competitors.gap: Not instant dispatch; takes 15%, 5% on recurring

competitors.name: Wag!
competitors.gap: US only; the on-demand model failed

competitors.name: Tailster
competitors.traction_note: About 1,050 Trustpilot reviews at 3.5; carer non-payment complaints

competitors.traction_note: General task marketplace with a dog-walking category

scenarios.name: Pessimistic
scenarios.note: 10 owners x 1.5 walks x GBP 2.84; GBP 400/month ads; liquidity never reached

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.note: 40 owners x 1.5 walks x GBP 2.84; ads GBP 600/month; budget gone in about 10 months

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.note: 150 owners x 1.5 walks x GBP 2.84; still loss-making before founder time

risks.risk: Walkers and owners move recurring walks off-platform
risks.mitigation: Charge walkers a subscription instead of a per-walk cut

risks.risk: Worker-status claim if the app sets prices and dispatches like Uber
risks.mitigation: Let walkers set prices and accept jobs freely

risks.risk: A lost or injured dog during a booked walk damages trust
risks.mitigation: Require walkers to hold care, custody and control cover

risks.risk: Borough licences and dog caps differ across London
risks.mitigation: Launch in one borough and check walker licences

test_plan.step: Write a one-page offer: booking, Stripe payments and GPS walk reports for walkers at GBP 19/month, with a pre-sale button
test_plan.verify: Page live with a working Stripe payment link

test_plan.step: Post in the NarpsUK Sitters Forum and 5 local walker Facebook groups; DM 40 London walkers
test_plan.verify: At least 5 replies asking for a call

test_plan.step: Run 5 calls: what they use today for bookings and payments, and what it costs
test_plan.verify: At least 3 of 5 name a paid tool or a pain they would pay to remove

test_plan.step: Ask each interested walker to pay for a founding seat
test_plan.verify: At least 3 paid seats at GBP 19/month
